newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's UM reports first half profits down 30 percent. [CORRECTED 17:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Belgium's UM reports first half profits down 30 percent. [CORRECTED 17:50 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects figure in headline to "30 percent" from "10 percent")

Belgian non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere SA (UM) said on Tuesday group net profit fell 29.9 (corrects from "9.6") percent to 218 (corrects from "281") million francs in the first half of this year against 311 million francs in the same 1995 period.
Current profit fell 30 percent to 782 million francs in the six months to June 30 from 1.11 billion in the first half of last year, the company said.

It said it was satisfied with the results of its recycling and copper and zinc refining activities, but disappointed by what it termed its transformation businesses which include cobalt, germanium and zinc sheet production.

This sector was badly hurt by the very depressed construction industry market in Germany, France and the Benelux countries in the early months of the year, Chief Executive Officer Karel Vinck told a news conference.

But Vinck said the major three-year restructuring programme the firm began implementing in January was well on course and that, all things being equal, results in the second half of the year would exceed those of the first half.
UM made a group net loss of 954 million francs in full year 1995 but a current profit of 1.8 billion.
The effects of the restructuring plan will not be felt at all in the 1996 results, but will begin to feed through from 1997 onwards, Vinvk said. ($1=31.09 Belgian Franc)
